mission: Iresh aftermath. Sela remains wary but respects Ben conditionally. Tavi survives but is shaken. Give Sela and Tavi an imperfect reunion: anger, relief, practical care, and no easy sentimentality. Talon suspects Ben’s holocron decision is not clean. Before they part, Talon gives Ben a plain future-call offer rather than a sentimental declaration: if Ben needs him, call. Talon frames it with reluctant humor - he will complain first, then come; if it involves prison food, Hutt paperwork, or dressing a Wookiee for a diplomatic reception, he is charging double.
why_now: The collapse is over, the Iresh operation is broken, and everyone who survived is on the plateau. This is the first quiet in days. Quiet is when the choices Ben has been deferring become real.
conflict: Talon knows Ben did not destroy the holocron. Sela knows Tavi is alive because of what Ben did in the lower basin, and what Ben did looked like something she does not have a good word for. Ben has the container in his belt and needs to decide what he is doing with it before he leaves Iresh.
turning_point: They return to Coruscant with the case mostly resolved and the dangerous knowledge unresolved.
closing_hook: They return to Coruscant with the case mostly resolved and the dangerous knowledge unresolved.
setting: Iresh, the eastern plateau pad and the cargo hauler's cold-lit cargo hold. Wind across the plateau carrying mineral dust and the smell of floodwater. Sela tends to Tavi against a supply crate. Ben and Talon talk near the ramp; the future-call offer happens here. Then transit lift-off through Iresh's overcast cloud layer into orbit.
emotional_trajectory: Do not rush away from Iresh. Resolve the local human stakes while making clear the moral danger has not ended. Reader-onboarding / clarity note: The holocron is not simply an evil object acquired. It is unfinished Jacen work: notes, methods, warnings, and dangerous knowledge that may also be useful. Ben’s omission begins here, before the coda.

stakes.personal: Ben’s justification for keeping the holocron is not dishonest — the knowledge might help, he is not ready to hand it to a system that buried it once already, destroying it improperly could release something, he needs to understand what is in it before he can be responsible about it. All of that is true. None of it is the whole story.
stakes.interpersonal: Talon’s future-call offer is plain and grounded and offered with deliberate humor — he will complain first, then come, and if it involves prison food, Hutt paperwork, or dressing a Wookiee for a diplomatic reception, he is charging double. It is the most serious thing he has said all novel, and he has disguised it as a joke so Ben does not have to handle it as a declaration.
stakes.external: They need to leave Iresh before Foundation-affiliated GA security arrives to assess the operation’s collapse. There is a narrow window before the legal situation becomes impossible again.

sensory_details: Wind across the eastern plateau carrying mineral dust and the smell of floodwater from the broken Glasswell below. The cargo hauler’s cold-lit hold. Sela tending to Tavi against a supply crate — not gently, not angrily, just efficiently, the way someone tends to family when they have been frightened and are now relieved and do not want to show it. The mineral-dust smell follows them into the hold.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Talon, near the ramp and watching Ben check the container's seal for the third time, says: 'You're not going to tell me you're destroying it.' Ben says it is complicated. Talon says: 'I know.' He does not push. The offer comes after that — 'If you need me, call' — framed as an inconvenience he will charge double for, which is the only way Talon can deliver sincerity without flinching.
turning_point_detail.shift: Ben does not destroy the holocron on Iresh. He places it in his belt pouch and they leave. The decision is made quietly, half-consciously, in the way that Ben's most dangerous choices arrive — as the only defensible option available.
turning_point_detail.cost: Talon will know the container went onto the hauler. Sela will watch them lift off and think of all the things offworlders take when they leave. The cost is not paid on Iresh. It is paid later.

emotional_arc.start: Ben is in aftermath mode: checking injuries, confirming the operation is broken, processing Sela and Tavi's reunion from a respectful distance. The container is in his hand but he has not made the decision consciously yet.
emotional_arc.shift: Talon's quiet, practical naming of what Ben is doing — not destroying the container — forces Ben to own the choice rather than drift into it. He chooses to keep it. He understands what that means.
emotional_arc.end: They lift off. Ben has the container and the decision and the beginning of the justification he will use for a long time. Talon has a future-call offer outstanding and a look that says: I see what you're doing. I'll still come if you call.

key_beats.beat_description: Sela and Tavi's imperfect reunion: Sela checks him for injuries while being audibly furious that he went in, which is not quite the same as blaming him, and Tavi does not argue back.
key_beats.state_change: The local human stakes are resolved — Tavi is alive and the sibling relationship is intact, imperfect, real.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the pull to stay near without interrupting; the specific aloneness of watching something private from the ramp

key_beats.beat_description: Ben checks on the wounded and stays near the hauler ramp rather than joining the reunion — correct instinct, but a lonely position.
key_beats.state_change: Ben marks his own distance from the human aftermath as appropriate — he is the outside party even after everything.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the recognition that staying back is right; the fact that it is right does not make it easier

key_beats.beat_description: Talon names the container situation plainly and quietly near the ramp: 'You're not going to tell me you're destroying it.'
key_beats.state_change: The decision Ben has been drifting through is made explicit — Talon sees it and names it without accusation.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the sentence landing before he has an answer; the absence of surprise at being seen

key_beats.beat_description: Ben chooses to keep the holocron; the decision arrives as a fact rather than a dramatic moment.
key_beats.state_change: The container stays in Ben's belt; the moral calculus is locked in rather than resolved.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the specific texture of a decision that feels defensible and incomplete at the same time; the justification starting to form

key_beats.beat_description: Talon offers a future-call — plain, grounded, framed as a complaint about expenses so that Ben does not have to receive it as a declaration.
key_beats.state_change: The partnership is not closed but placed on a voluntary footing; Talon makes the offer in the only register that both of them can handle.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the humor landing as what it is; the seriousness arriving through it rather than despite it
